title: Symmetric localization of $ν_{\text{tot}}=4/3$ fractional topological insulator edges
summary: Motivated by the recent twisted MoTe$_2$ experiment [arXiv:2601.18508], we develop a disordered interacting edge theory of a fractional topological insulator at $ν_{\text{tot}}=4/3$, consisting of two time-reversal-conjugated $ν=2/3$ fractional quantum Hall states. For an $S_z$-conserving edge, we uncover three distinct phases with two possible conductance values per edge in the long-edge limit: $\frac{2}{3}\frac{e^2}{h}$ and $\frac{4}{3}\frac{e^2}{h}$. In the presence of $S_z$-changing perturbations (e.g., Rashba spin-orbit coupling), an interaction-induced insulating edge state can emerge without breaking time-reversal or charge-conservation symmetry, corresponding to the absence of a topologically protected edge state. We further provide an exact mapping to a noninteracting fermionic theory exhibiting Anderson localization. Our results showcase an explicit, experimentally relevant example that the edge-state two-terminal transport is insufficient to identify the $ν_{\text{tot}}=4/3$ fractional topological insulators.

AI.tldr: Fractional topological insulator edge theory at ν_tot=4/3 shows multiple conductance phases, including interaction-induced insulating edge without symmetry breaking, challenging transport-based identification.
AI.motivation: Motivated by recent twisted MoTe2 experiments, the paper aims to understand the edge physics of fractional topological insulators at ν_tot=4/3, particularly how disorder and interactions affect edge transport and topological protection.
AI.method: Developed a disordered interacting edge theory for a ν_tot=4/3 fractional topological insulator consisting of two time-reversal-conjugated ν=2/3 fractional quantum Hall states. Analyzed both Sz-conserving and Sz-changing perturbations, and provided an exact mapping to a noninteracting fermionic theory exhibiting Anderson localization.
AI.result: Found three distinct phases with two possible conductance values per edge (2/3 e²/h and 4/3 e²/h) in Sz-conserving case. With Sz-changing perturbations, discovered an interaction-induced insulating edge state emerges without breaking time-reversal or charge-conservation symmetry. Provided exact mapping to noninteracting fermionic Anderson localization theory.
AI.conclusion: Two-terminal transport measurements alone are insufficient to identify ν_tot=4/3 fractional topological insulators due to the possibility of interaction-induced insulating edge states that preserve all symmetries, challenging conventional transport-based topological classification.

title: Classical Kitaev model in a magnetic field
summary: Motivated by experiments on spin-orbit coupled magnets with Kitaev exchange in magnetic fields, we present an analysis of the classical Kitaev honeycomb model in the presence of a magnetic field. We show that there is a spin liquid regime that exists within a finite window of fields from zero up to a finite threshold before transitioning into the polarized paramagnet. We uncover constraints that spins need to satisfy in the ground state and show that they determine the exact limiting zero temperature behavior of the heat capacity and magnetic susceptibility within the spin liquid as a function of field. When the field is finite, both the two-point spin and the quadrupolar correlations are short-ranged, in contrast to the zero-field case. We rationalize an effective mass for the quadrupolar correlations in terms of a coarse-grained theory with fluctuating effective charge degrees of freedom. Finally, we show that weak site-dilution does not change the magnetization within the spin liquid -- a kind of "perfect" compensation of the site dilution.

AI.tldr: Classical Kitaev honeycomb model in magnetic field shows finite spin liquid regime, exact thermodynamic behavior, short-range correlations, and perfect compensation against site dilution.
AI.motivation: Motivated by experiments on spin-orbit coupled magnets with Kitaev exchange in magnetic fields, to understand the classical Kitaev honeycomb model under magnetic field conditions.
AI.method: Analysis of classical Kitaev honeycomb model in magnetic field, uncovering ground state constraints, calculating exact limiting zero-temperature behavior of heat capacity and susceptibility, studying correlation functions, developing coarse-grained theory for quadrupolar correlations, and investigating site-dilution effects.
AI.result: Finite spin liquid regime exists from zero field up to threshold before polarized paramagnet transition; exact zero-temperature thermodynamic behavior determined; finite field yields short-range spin and quadrupolar correlations (contrasting zero-field case); effective mass for quadrupolar correlations rationalized; weak site-dilution shows perfect compensation within spin liquid.
AI.conclusion: Classical Kitaev model in magnetic field exhibits robust spin liquid phase with exact thermodynamic properties, short-range correlations, and remarkable stability against site dilution, providing insights for experimental spin-orbit coupled magnets.

title: Disorder-induced localisation in the Mott-Hubbard model
summary: For the Fermi-Hubbard model in the Mott insulator phase, we employ the hierarchy of correlations to study how doublon and holon quasi-particle excitations are affected by adding disorder to the system. We study two types of disorder: charge disorder, in the form of on-site potential randomness; and spin disorder, in the form of a fixed, randomly generated background spin arrangement. By analysing the quasi-particle eigen-spectra and quantifying the degree to which the corresponding eigen-states localise, we find both an energetic and spatial separation between localised and delocalised states in the charge disorder. In contrast, the spin disorder results in localised states throughout the quasi-particle bands. Finally, we repeat our calculations using strong-coupling perturbation theory, and compare the results obtained from both methods.

AI.tldr: Study of doublon and holon quasi-particle excitations in disordered Mott insulator phase of Fermi-Hubbard model using hierarchy of correlations and strong-coupling perturbation theory.
AI.motivation: To understand how disorder affects doublon and holon quasi-particle excitations in the Mott insulator phase of the Fermi-Hubbard model, specifically examining different types of disorder and their impact on localization properties.
AI.method: Employed hierarchy of correlations method to study quasi-particle excitations under two types of disorder: charge disorder (on-site potential randomness) and spin disorder (fixed random background spin arrangement). Analyzed quasi-particle eigen-spectra and quantified eigen-state localization. Compared results with strong-coupling perturbation theory calculations.
AI.result: For charge disorder, found both energetic and spatial separation between localized and delocalized states. For spin disorder, found localized states throughout the quasi-particle bands. Results from hierarchy of correlations and strong-coupling perturbation theory were compared.
AI.conclusion: Different types of disorder (charge vs. spin) lead to distinct localization behaviors in doublon and holon quasi-particle excitations in the Mott insulator phase, with charge disorder showing separation between localized and delocalized states while spin disorder results in complete localization throughout bands.

title: Long-range magnetic order with disordered spin orientations in a high-entropy antiferromagnet
comment: 10 pages, plus references, 1 table, 4 figures, and Supplementary information, accepted for publication in Nature Communications
summary: Disorder in magnetic systems typically suppresses long-range order, promoting short-range states such as spin glasses and magnetic clusters. This is particularly prominent in high-entropy materials, characterized by the random distributions of local magnetic entities and exchange interactions. However, in rare exceptions, long-range magnetic order can persist in high-entropy systems, while the microscopic characters and underlying mechanisms remain elusive, especially the magnetic behaviors of individual elements. Here, combining neutron diffraction and resonant soft x-ray scattering, we have conducted an element-specific investigation into the magnetic order of a high-entropy honeycomb-lattice van der Waals material (Mn1/4Fe1/4Co1/4Ni1/4)PS3. Despite significant atomic disorder, long-range zigzag antiferromagnetic order is observed below 72 K, with all four transition-metal elements participating in a unified phase transition. However, the spin orientations of various elements are distinct, attributed to the competition between single-ion anisotropies and exchange interactions. Our findings showcase a novel form of long-range magnetic order with disordered spin orientations, which is synergically stabilized by distinct magnetic elements in a high entropy magnet, offering a new paradigm for understanding complex magnetic systems.

AI.tldr: High-entropy honeycomb van der Waals material (Mn1/4Fe1/4Co1/4Ni1/4)PS3 exhibits long-range zigzag antiferromagnetic order despite atomic disorder, with all four transition metals participating in a unified phase transition but with distinct spin orientations.
AI.motivation: To understand how long-range magnetic order can persist in high-entropy systems despite significant atomic disorder, and to investigate the element-specific magnetic behaviors and underlying mechanisms in such complex magnetic systems.
AI.method: Combined neutron diffraction and resonant soft x-ray scattering for element-specific investigation of magnetic order in high-entropy honeycomb-lattice van der Waals material (Mn1/4Fe1/4Co1/4Ni1/4)PS3.
AI.result: Long-range zigzag antiferromagnetic order observed below 72 K with all four transition-metal elements participating in a unified phase transition, but with distinct spin orientations attributed to competition between single-ion anisotropies and exchange interactions.
AI.conclusion: Discovery of a novel form of long-range magnetic order with disordered spin orientations, synergically stabilized by distinct magnetic elements in a high-entropy magnet, offering a new paradigm for understanding complex magnetic systems.

title: Persistent short-range charge correlations revealed by ultrafast melting of electronic order in YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{6+x}$
summary: Charge density waves (CDW) are ubiquitous in the complex phase diagram of cuprate superconductors and exhibit both short- and long-range correlations. Using time-resolved resonant X-ray scattering, we investigate the photo-induced dynamics of CDW in YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{6.67}$. We discover an excitation threshold ($Φ$$_\mathrm{C}$ $\approx$ 65 $μ$J/cm$^2$) above which long-range CDW disappear, revealing a persistent CDW peak with short-range correlation length. Ultrafast photo-excitation promptly uncovers this residual short-range CDW correlations, appearing within $\approx$ 0.2 ps. Long-range CDW coherence recovers within $\approx$ 0.6 ps, while the peak intensity remains partially suppressed. We rationalize the dichotomic behavior in the fluence and temporal dependencies as the signature of two coexisting CDW peaks, arising from short- and long-range correlations, which we disentangle through their distinct response to photo-excitation. We provide evidence that the collapse of long-range correlations is driven by an electronic process, while short-range correlations are characterized by distinct timescales and stiffness against photo-excitation. This approach establishes ultrafast X-ray scattering as an effective tool for disentangling coexisting density waves and correlations in quantum materials.

AI.tldr: Ultrafast X-ray scattering reveals two coexisting CDW components in YBa2Cu3O6.67: short-range correlations that persist above excitation threshold and long-range correlations that collapse above 65 μJ/cm² but recover within 0.6 ps.
AI.motivation: To understand the photo-induced dynamics of charge density waves in cuprate superconductors and disentangle coexisting short- and long-range CDW correlations using time-resolved techniques.
AI.method: Time-resolved resonant X-ray scattering on YBa2Cu3O6.67 with ultrafast photo-excitation, measuring CDW response across fluence and temporal domains to separate short- and long-range correlation components.
AI.result: Discovery of excitation threshold (ΦC ≈ 65 μJ/cm²) above which long-range CDW disappear, revealing persistent short-range CDW peak. Short-range correlations appear within ≈0.2 ps, long-range coherence recovers within ≈0.6 ps with partial intensity suppression.
AI.conclusion: Two coexisting CDW peaks with distinct responses: long-range correlations collapse via electronic process, short-range correlations show different timescales and stiffness. Ultrafast X-ray scattering effectively disentangles coexisting density waves in quantum materials.

title: ALD Oxidant as A Tuning Knob for Memory Window Expansion in Ferroelectric FETs for Vertical NAND Applications
summary: Dielectric inserts are widely used to expand the memory window (MW) in ferroelectric FETs (FeFETs) for vertical NAND applications, with prior efforts focused primarily on material selection and stack positioning. Here, we demonstrate that the ALD oxidant used for the Al2O3 interlayer serves as a process-level tuning knob for MW engineering. H2O-grown Al2O3 yields a significantly larger MW (7-8 V) compared to O3 (4 V) for both gate-injection (12/3) and tunnel dielectric (8/3/8) configurations. While the tunnel dielectric (8/3/8) stack maintains robust retention up to 1e4s at 125C despite the larger MW, the gate-injection (12/3) configuration exhibits pronounced retention degradation for the H2O case. The enhanced MW is attributed to higher interlayer leakage associated with H2O-based ALD. These results establish oxidant choice as a key process parameter for co-optimizing MW and retention in ferroelectric NAND technologies.

AI.tldr: ALD oxidant choice (H2O vs O3) for Al2O3 interlayer significantly impacts memory window in FeFETs, with H2O providing larger MW but affecting retention differently based on stack configuration.
AI.motivation: Dielectric inserts are used to expand memory window in FeFETs for vertical NAND, but prior work focused on material selection and stack positioning. This paper investigates ALD oxidant as a process-level tuning knob for MW engineering.
AI.method: Comparative study of H2O-grown vs O3-grown Al2O3 interlayers in ferroelectric FETs, examining both gate-injection (12/3) and tunnel dielectric (8/3/8) configurations. Analysis of memory window, retention characteristics, and interlayer leakage.
AI.result: H2O-grown Al2O3 yields significantly larger memory window (7-8 V) compared to O3 (4 V) for both configurations. Tunnel dielectric stack maintains robust retention up to 1e4s at 125°C despite larger MW, while gate-injection configuration exhibits pronounced retention degradation for H2O case.
AI.conclusion: ALD oxidant choice (H2O vs O3) is a key process parameter for co-optimizing memory window and retention in ferroelectric NAND technologies, with H2O providing larger MW but requiring careful stack design consideration for retention.

title: Ab initio quantum embedding description of magic angle twisted bilayer graphene at even-integer fillings
summary: Magic angle twisted bilayer graphene (MATBG) hosts narrow moiré bands with meV-scale energy splittings, making its correlated phases sensitive to both material parameters and modeling choices in low-energy downfolding. We develop an ab initio quantum-embedding workflow that derives interacting flat-band Hamiltonians from Kohn-Sham density functional theory (KS-DFT) of a relaxed, unstrained structure. Our model combines constrained random phase approximation (cRPA) screening, controlled double-counting subtraction, and an automated gauge-fixing procedure based on the selected columns of the density matrix (SCDM) that is compatible with symmetry-resolved many-body calculations. Solving the resulting models using Hartree-Fock (HF) and coupled cluster singles and doubles (CCSD), we recover robust insulating Kramers intervalley coherent (KIVC) states at charge neutrality ($ν=0$) and at electron doping ($ν=+2$). The main new physical effect appears on the hole-doped side: at $ν=-2$ we observe a fragile semimetal with a weak $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ Kekulé modulation and enhanced intervalley-scattering peaks in the Fourier-transformed local density of states. Although the underlying KS-DFT band structure is nearly particle-hole symmetric, the effective interacting Hamiltonian exhibits a pronounced particle-hole asymmetry at $ν=\pm 2$ that we trace to momentum-dependent single-particle renormalizations generated by subtraction terms constructed from reference densities consistent with the KS-DFT filling. Our work provides a first-principles route for connecting microscopic electronic structure, screened interactions, subtraction choices, and scanning tunneling microscopy signatures in MATBG.

AI.tldr: Ab initio quantum-embedding workflow derives interacting flat-band Hamiltonians for magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, revealing robust KIVC insulators at ν=0,+2 and fragile semimetal with Kekulé modulation at ν=-2, showing pronounced particle-hole asymmetry despite nearly symmetric DFT bands.
AI.motivation: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene hosts narrow moiré bands with meV-scale energy splittings, making its correlated phases sensitive to both material parameters and modeling choices in low-energy downfolding. There's a need to connect microscopic electronic structure, screened interactions, subtraction choices, and experimental signatures like scanning tunneling microscopy.
AI.method: Developed an ab initio quantum-embedding workflow that derives interacting flat-band Hamiltonians from Kohn-Sham DFT of relaxed, unstrained structure. Combines constrained random phase approximation (cRPA) screening, controlled double-counting subtraction, and automated gauge-fixing procedure based on selected columns of the density matrix (SCDM) compatible with symmetry-resolved many-body calculations.
AI.result: Recover robust insulating Kramers intervalley coherent (KIVC) states at charge neutrality (ν=0) and at electron doping (ν=+2). At hole-doped side (ν=-2), observe fragile semimetal with weak √3×√3 Kekulé modulation and enhanced intervalley-scattering peaks in Fourier-transformed local density of states. Despite nearly particle-hole symmetric KS-DFT band structure, effective interacting Hamiltonian exhibits pronounced particle-hole asymmetry at ν=±2 due to momentum-dependent single-particle renormalizations from subtraction terms.
AI.conclusion: Provides a first-principles route for connecting microscopic electronic structure, screened interactions, subtraction choices, and scanning tunneling microscopy signatures in MATBG. The workflow enables systematic study of correlated phases with controlled approximations from ab initio calculations.

title: Pauli-limited upper critical field and anisotropic depairing effect of La2.82Sr0.18Ni2O7 superconducting thin film
summary: We investigate the upper critical field and superconducting anisotropy of epitaxial La2.82Sr0.18Ni2O7 thin films, which show a sharp superconducting transition at Tc=31.6 K. Near Tc, superconductivity exhibits thickness-limited two-dimensional characteristics. Upon cooling, the out-of-plane coherence length decreases below the sample thickness of 6 nm, corresponding to a 3-unit-cell film, indicating a crossover to intrinsic three-dimensional bulk superconductivity. High-field transport measurements reveal large upper critical fields with a small anisotropy ratio gama~1.34, comparable to bulk Ruddlesden-Popper nickelates. At low temperatures, the in-plane (ab) upper critical field Hc2(ab) is strongly suppressed by spin-paramagnetic pair breaking and approaches the Pauli limit (Hc2(Pauli)=58 T), while Hc2(c) remains largely unaffected. This anisotropic Pauli limitation accounts for the reduced upper critical field anisotropy and supports the conclusion that superconductivity in these films is fundamentally three-dimensional bulk like. Our results highlight the essential role of spin-paramagnetic effects in shaping the high-field superconducting phase diagram of Ruddlesden-Popper nickelates.

AI.tldr: La2.82Sr0.18Ni2O7 thin films show 3D bulk superconductivity with small anisotropy (γ~1.34), where spin-paramagnetic pair breaking suppresses in-plane upper critical field near Pauli limit, revealing essential role of spin effects in nickelate superconductivity.
AI.motivation: To investigate the dimensionality crossover and upper critical field behavior in epitaxial La2.82Sr0.18Ni2O7 thin films, particularly understanding how spin-paramagnetic effects shape the superconducting phase diagram in Ruddlesden-Popper nickelates.
AI.method: Study of epitaxial La2.82Sr0.18Ni2O7 thin films with Tc=31.6 K using high-field transport measurements to determine upper critical fields Hc2(ab) and Hc2(c), analyzing thickness-dependent dimensionality crossover from 2D to 3D behavior through coherence length measurements.
AI.result: Films show thickness-limited 2D superconductivity near Tc but crossover to intrinsic 3D bulk superconductivity upon cooling. Small anisotropy ratio γ~1.34 comparable to bulk nickelates. Hc2(ab) strongly suppressed by spin-paramagnetic pair breaking approaching Pauli limit (58 T), while Hc2(c) remains unaffected, explaining reduced anisotropy.
AI.conclusion: Superconductivity in La2.82Sr0.18Ni2O7 films is fundamentally three-dimensional bulk-like, with spin-paramagnetic effects playing essential role in shaping high-field superconducting phase diagram of Ruddlesden-Popper nickelates through anisotropic Pauli limitation.

title: Endohedral Derivatives of the Recently Synthesized Two-Dimensional Fullerene Networks: Electronic and Optical Insights from First-Principles Calculations
summary: The quasi-hexagonal phase of the two-dimensional fullerene network (qHPC$_{60}$), recently synthesized, has emerged as a stable carbon-based material with distinct structural and electronic features. In this work, we employed density functional theory (DFT) calculations to investigate the electronic and optical properties of its endohedral derivatives. The encapsulation of nitrogen, cerium, and strontium atoms inside fullerene cages was systematically analyzed at different concentrations. Our results show that encapsulation preserves the semiconducting backbone of pristine qHPC$_{60}$ while introducing localized electronic states that alter the bandgap and enable new transition channels. Nitrogen encapsulation produces intragap states with potential relevance for discrete optical emission, whereas cerium and strontium generate intraband states near the conduction edge. These modifications induce a red shift of the absorption onset into the visible spectrum, accompanied by enhanced refractive and absorptive responses. The robustness of the electronic structure under reduced concentrations indicates that the fully encapsulated limit adequately represents the system. Overall, the findings highlight impurity-endowed qHPC$_{60}$ as a promising platform for optoelectronic and light-harvesting applications.

AI.tldr: DFT study shows that encapsulating N, Ce, and Sr atoms in quasi-hexagonal fullerene network (qHPC₆₀) preserves its semiconducting backbone while introducing localized states that modify bandgaps and optical properties, making it promising for optoelectronics.
AI.motivation: To investigate how endohedral encapsulation of different atoms (N, Ce, Sr) affects the electronic and optical properties of the recently synthesized quasi-hexagonal phase of 2D fullerene network (qHPC₆₀), exploring its potential for optoelectronic applications.
AI.method: Employed density functional theory (DFT) calculations to systematically analyze the electronic and optical properties of endohedral derivatives of qHPC₆₀ with encapsulated nitrogen, cerium, and strontium atoms at different concentrations.
AI.result: Encapsulation preserves the semiconducting backbone while introducing localized electronic states: N creates intragap states for potential discrete optical emission; Ce and Sr generate intraband states near conduction edge. These modifications cause red shift of absorption onset into visible spectrum and enhanced refractive/absorptive responses. Electronic structure remains robust at reduced concentrations.
AI.conclusion: Impurity-endowed qHPC₆₀ represents a promising platform for optoelectronic and light-harvesting applications due to tunable electronic properties and enhanced optical responses achieved through endohedral encapsulation of various atoms.

title: Observation of Kondo hybridization wave in UTe2
summary: Condensed matter systems with strong electronic correlations often manifest a variety of intertwined ordered phases of charge, spin, orbital and other degrees of freedom. As a prototypical strongly correlated electronic system, the Kondo lattice provides fertile soil for many fascinating quantum states, including quantum criticality, unconventional superconductivity, hidden order and topological Kondo insulator/semimetal. The foundation of Kondo physics lies in the hybridization between localized moments and itinerant electrons. Generally, the evolution of Kondo hybridization is characterized as a broad crossover rather than a phase transition. Thus far, an ordered hybridization phase has not been observed. Here, we use scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) to identify a translational-symmetry-breaking order of Kondo hybridization wave(KHW) for the first time on the surface of the spin-triplet heavy-fermion superconductor UTe2. The unprecedented phase of KHW manifests as a periodically modulated Fano lattice, accompanied by a commensurate charge density wave (CDW) and a pronounced energy gap opening near the Fermi level. This KHW-imprinted CDW has an intriguing real-space texture of complementary occupation of the heavy f and conduction charges, thereby forming a Kondo superlattice. The KHW is coexistent with superconductivity in UTe2, which may provide valuable insight into its controversial spin-triplet pairing symmetry and the underlying mechanism. Our first experimental evidence for an ordered hybridization state potentially sheds new light on the strong correlation physics of Kondo lattice system.

AI.tldr: First experimental observation of an ordered Kondo hybridization wave (KHW) phase in UTe2, manifested as a periodically modulated Fano lattice with a commensurate charge density wave and energy gap near Fermi level, coexisting with superconductivity.
AI.motivation: Despite extensive study of Kondo lattice systems, an ordered hybridization phase has never been observed. The evolution of Kondo hybridization is typically characterized as a broad crossover rather than a phase transition. This work aims to identify and characterize such an ordered state in the spin-triplet heavy-fermion superconductor UTe2.
AI.method: Scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) was used to investigate the surface of UTe2. The technique enabled identification of a translational-symmetry-breaking order of Kondo hybridization wave, manifested as a periodically modulated Fano lattice with accompanying charge density wave and energy gap measurements.
AI.result: Discovery of an unprecedented phase of Kondo hybridization wave (KHW) that breaks translational symmetry. The KHW appears as a periodically modulated Fano lattice accompanied by a commensurate charge density wave and a pronounced energy gap opening near the Fermi level. The KHW-imprinted CDW exhibits complementary occupation of heavy f and conduction charges, forming a Kondo superlattice. The KHW coexists with superconductivity in UTe2.
AI.conclusion: This work provides the first experimental evidence for an ordered hybridization state in a Kondo lattice system. The coexistence of KHW with superconductivity in UTe2 may offer valuable insights into its controversial spin-triplet pairing symmetry and the underlying mechanism. The discovery potentially sheds new light on strong correlation physics in Kondo lattice systems.

title: Gap structure and phase diagram of twisted bilayer cuprates from a microscopic perspective
summary: Since the prediction of a time-reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB) $d+id^\prime$ state in twisted bilayer cuprate superconductors by Can et al. in 2021, several experiments have attempted to detect this state, yielding conflicting results. At present, it is not clear which differences in samples or experimental conditions might explain these discrepancies. In this work, we perform a tight-binding lattice model calculation with phenomenological interlayer tunneling, examining the order parameter as a function of twist angle, interlayer tunneling, doping, and temperature. We observe the TRSB state to be correlated to the position of the Van Hove singularity in the normal state which changes not only as a function of doping but also the tunneling strength. Two such phases are identified as nominally consistent with in-plane $d+id'$ and $d+is$ order, but with unexpected transformation properties under bilayer symmetry operations. We calculate the Josephson critical current, in particular examining the angle dependence for various tunneling strengths. Finally, we discuss the existing experiments in the context of our results.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates the controversial time-reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB) d+id' state in twisted bilayer cuprates, analyzing how twist angle, tunneling, doping, and temperature affect the order parameter, and connecting the TRSB state to Van Hove singularity positions.
AI.motivation: Since the 2021 prediction of TRSB d+id' state in twisted bilayer cuprates, conflicting experimental results have emerged without clear understanding of what sample differences or experimental conditions explain these discrepancies.
AI.method: Tight-binding lattice model calculations with phenomenological interlayer tunneling, examining order parameter as function of twist angle, interlayer tunneling strength, doping, and temperature.
AI.result: TRSB state correlates with Van Hove singularity position in normal state, which changes with both doping and tunneling strength. Two phases identified as nominally consistent with in-plane d+id' and d+is order but with unexpected transformation properties under bilayer symmetry operations. Josephson critical current angle dependence calculated for various tunneling strengths.
AI.conclusion: The work provides theoretical framework to understand conflicting experimental results by identifying key parameters (Van Hove singularity position, tunneling strength) that control TRSB state emergence, and discusses existing experiments in context of these findings.

title: Intertwined Swirling Polarization States in BaTiO$_3$ with Embedded BaZrO$_3$ Nanoregions
comment: Accepted for publication in Phys. Rev. Lett
summary: Ferroelectric materials embedded with dielectric inclusions offer a unique platform for exploring novel topological polar textures. Using first-principles-based atomistic simulations, we investigate the polarization behavior of a BaTiO$_3$ matrix containing segregated BaZrO$_3$ nanoregions. We demonstrate that the polar texture in three-dimensionally ordered arrays of dielectric inclusions is governed by their size and spacing, revealing three distinct regimes. At large separations, the nanocomposite exhibits bulk-like BaTiO3 phase transitions, while at smaller spacings, interconnected swirling polarization patterns give rise to vortex supercrystal states. We analyze the stabilization mechanisms of these states and show that each regime is characterized by distinct switching behavior. Furthermore, we find that nanocomposites with randomly distributed dielectric inclusions exhibit swirling polarization textures, giving rise to an amorphous network of entangled vortices. Our findings provide new insights into the physics of relaxor ferroelectrics, are consistent with recent experimental observations, and open up new possibilities for designing materials with emergent topological functionalities.

AI.tldr: BaTiO₃ matrix with BaZrO₃ dielectric inclusions exhibits size/spacing-dependent polarization regimes including vortex supercrystals and amorphous vortex networks, offering insights into relaxor ferroelectrics and topological functionalities.
AI.motivation: To explore novel topological polar textures in ferroelectric-dielectric nanocomposites and understand the physics of relaxor ferroelectrics through polarization behavior in structured dielectric inclusions.
AI.method: First-principles-based atomistic simulations of BaTiO₃ matrix containing segregated BaZrO₃ nanoregions, analyzing both three-dimensionally ordered arrays and randomly distributed inclusions.
AI.result: Three distinct regimes based on inclusion size and spacing: 1) large separations show bulk-like BaTiO₃ phase transitions, 2) smaller spacings produce interconnected swirling patterns forming vortex supercrystals, 3) random distributions create amorphous networks of entangled vortices. Each regime exhibits distinct switching behavior.
AI.conclusion: The findings provide new insights into relaxor ferroelectric physics, align with recent experimental observations, and enable design of materials with emergent topological functionalities through controlled dielectric inclusion engineering.

title: Formulation of intrinsic nonlinear thermal conductivity for bosonic systems using quantum kinetic equation
summary: Nonlinear responses in transport phenomena have attracted significant attention because they can arise even when linear responses are forbidden by symmetry, with the quantum geometry of Bloch wave functions playing an essential role. While such effects have been extensively studied in electric transport, similar quantum-geometric mechanisms are also expected to govern nonlinear thermal transport. In particular, thermal responses are crucial in bosonic systems such as magnons and phonons, which are charge-neutral quasiparticles. However, a consistent theoretical description of nonlinear thermal transport remains challenging because of the difficulty in the treatment of energy magnetization in higher-order responses with Luttinger's gravitational potential method. Here, we formulate the intrinsic nonlinear thermal conductivity of bosonic systems using a quantum kinetic equation approach that avoids Luttinger's method and naturally incorporates contributions from energy magnetization. We identify three distinct contributions to the nonlinear thermal conductivity: two expressed in terms of quantum-geometric quantities, namely the quantum metric and the thermal Berry-connection polarizability (TBCP), and a third determined solely by the band dispersions. Applying our formalism to a specific quantum spin model within linear spin-wave theory, we show that the TBCP term dominates the nonlinear thermal Hall effect in the absence of threefold symmetry. Our results differ quantitatively from those obtained using semiclassical theory, thereby highlighting the importance of quantum corrections beyond the semiclassical picture. These findings establish a general framework for intrinsic nonlinear thermal responses in bosonic systems and reveal quantum-geometric mechanisms underlying thermal transport beyond linear response theory.

AI.tldr: The paper formulates intrinsic nonlinear thermal conductivity for bosonic systems using quantum kinetic equations, identifying three contributions: quantum metric, thermal Berry-connection polarizability, and band dispersion terms, with applications showing quantum corrections beyond semiclassical theory.
AI.motivation: Nonlinear thermal transport in bosonic systems (magnons, phonons) lacks consistent theoretical description due to difficulties treating energy magnetization in higher-order responses with Luttinger's gravitational potential method, despite quantum-geometric mechanisms being expected to govern such effects similar to electric transport.
AI.method: Developed a quantum kinetic equation approach that avoids Luttinger's method and naturally incorporates energy magnetization contributions. Formulated intrinsic nonlinear thermal conductivity with three distinct contributions: quantum metric, thermal Berry-connection polarizability (TBCP), and band dispersion terms.
AI.result: Applied formalism to a quantum spin model within linear spin-wave theory, showing TBCP term dominates nonlinear thermal Hall effect in absence of threefold symmetry. Results differ quantitatively from semiclassical theory, highlighting importance of quantum corrections beyond semiclassical picture.
AI.conclusion: Establishes general framework for intrinsic nonlinear thermal responses in bosonic systems, revealing quantum-geometric mechanisms underlying thermal transport beyond linear response theory and demonstrating significant quantum corrections to semiclassical predictions.

title: Supercurrents in Josephson junctions with chiral molecular potentials
summary: The influence of chiral molecular potentials on phase-coherent transport in superconducting Josephson junctions is investigated. Within a Bogoliubov-de Gennes tight-binding framework, an SNS junction functionalized by adsorbed chiral molecules is modeled, where electrostatic gradients generated by the molecules induce spin-orbit coupling in the normal region. The equilibrium charge current-phase relation is found to remain largely insensitive to molecular chirality in symmetric, zero-field configurations. In contrast, the spin supercurrent exhibits a pronounced chirality-dependent response, with opposite enantiomers producing distinct and anisotropic spin-polarized Josephson currents. The resulting handedness contrast can be enhanced through control parameters such as molecular orientation and the strength of the induced spin-orbit coupling. The temperature dependence of these currents further shows that the chirality-dependent signatures persist across a range of temperatures well below the superconducting critical temperature. These results establish Josephson interferometry as a phase-sensitive and accessible platform for detecting molecular chirality and highlight spin-polarized superconducting transport as a promising route toward integrating chiral molecular functionality into superconducting spintronic devices.

AI.tldr: Chiral molecules adsorbed on SNS Josephson junctions induce spin-orbit coupling, generating chirality-dependent spin supercurrents but not affecting charge currents in symmetric configurations.
AI.motivation: To investigate how chiral molecular potentials influence phase-coherent transport in superconducting Josephson junctions and explore the potential for detecting molecular chirality through superconducting transport phenomena.
AI.method: Bogoliubov-de Gennes tight-binding framework modeling of SNS junctions functionalized by adsorbed chiral molecules, where electrostatic gradients from molecules induce spin-orbit coupling in the normal region.
AI.result: Charge current-phase relation remains insensitive to molecular chirality in symmetric zero-field configurations, but spin supercurrent shows pronounced chirality-dependent response with opposite enantiomers producing distinct anisotropic spin-polarized Josephson currents. Chirality contrast can be enhanced via molecular orientation and spin-orbit coupling strength, with signatures persisting across temperatures below Tc.
AI.conclusion: Josephson interferometry serves as a phase-sensitive platform for detecting molecular chirality, and spin-polarized superconducting transport offers promising route for integrating chiral molecular functionality into superconducting spintronic devices.

title: Bias in Universal Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials and its Effects on Fine-Tuning
summary: Universal machine learned interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) embody a growing area of interest due to their transferability across the periodic table, displaying an error of about 0.6 kcal/mol against the Matbench Discovery test set. However, we show that achieving more accurate predictions on out-of-domain tasks requires fine-tuning. Additionally, we investigate the existence and influence of model biases in molecular dynamics (MD) by examining two approaches for data generation: from multiple MD trajectories in parallel, which we call naive fine-tuning, and from a single MD trajectory with fine-tuning after set intervals, which we call periodic fine-tuning. Our results find that naive fine-tuning generates constrained datasets that fail to represent MD simulations, and thus downstream fine-tuned models fail during extrapolation. In contrast, periodic fine-tuning yields models which are more generalizable and accurate, producing low-error dynamics. These findings indicate the role of uMLIP bias in fine-tuning, and highlights the need for multiple fine-tuning steps. Lastly, we relate unphysical behavior to principal component space, and quantify extrapolations through Q-residual analysis, which are useful as a proxy for epistemic uncertainty for larger simulations.

AI.tldr: Universal ML interatomic potentials achieve ~0.6 kcal/mol error but require fine-tuning for out-of-domain tasks; periodic fine-tuning outperforms naive fine-tuning for generalizability in MD simulations.
AI.motivation: Universal machine learned interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) show good transferability but require investigation of fine-tuning strategies for improved accuracy on out-of-domain tasks and understanding of model biases in molecular dynamics simulations.
AI.method: Examined two fine-tuning approaches: 1) naive fine-tuning from multiple MD trajectories in parallel, and 2) periodic fine-tuning from a single MD trajectory with fine-tuning at intervals. Used principal component space analysis and Q-residual analysis to quantify extrapolations and epistemic uncertainty.
AI.result: Naive fine-tuning generates constrained datasets that fail to represent MD simulations, causing downstream models to fail during extrapolation. Periodic fine-tuning yields more generalizable and accurate models with low-error dynamics. Q-residual analysis serves as a proxy for epistemic uncertainty in larger simulations.
AI.conclusion: uMLIPs require multiple fine-tuning steps for optimal performance; periodic fine-tuning strategy is superior for generalizability; model biases significantly influence fine-tuning outcomes; Q-residual analysis provides useful uncertainty quantification for extrapolative simulations.

title: Theory of Many-Body Multipole Operators in Single-Centered Electron Systems: Two-Body Toroidal Monopoles in Spinless Orbitals
comment: 5 pages in the main text, plus 100 pages of supplemental material
summary: One-body multipole operators are defined as irreducible representations of rotational symmetry together with spatial-inversion and time-reversal symmetries, providing a systematic framework for classifying electronic internal degrees of freedom and for describing a wide variety of composite order parameters. While this formalism has been successfully established for the one-body operator space, a systematic classification of the many-body operator space, especially in interacting systems, remains an open challenge. In this paper, we extend the multipole formalism in the one-body operator space to the many-body operator space. By formulating fermionic creation and annihilation operators as spherical tensors and employing Clebsch-Gordan coupling combined with the exterior (Grassmann) algebra, we construct an irreducible decomposition of many-body operators that fully incorporates fermionic antisymmetrization. As a concrete application, we classify monopoles appearing in spinless many-body operators. In particular, we show that the electric toroidal monopole, a pseudoscalar breaking spatial-inversion symmetry, and the magnetic toroidal monopole, a time reversal-odd scalar, become active in spinless interacting many-body systems, although they are absent in the spinless one-body hybrid orbital space.

AI.tldr: Extends multipole formalism from one-body to many-body operator space using fermionic spherical tensors and Clebsch-Gordan coupling with Grassmann algebra, enabling systematic classification of many-body operators in interacting systems.
AI.motivation: While one-body multipole operators are well-established for classifying electronic degrees of freedom and composite order parameters, a systematic classification of many-body operator space in interacting systems remains an open challenge that needs to be addressed.
AI.method: Formulates fermionic creation/annihilation operators as spherical tensors and employs Clebsch-Gordan coupling combined with exterior (Grassmann) algebra to construct irreducible decomposition of many-body operators with full fermionic antisymmetrization.
AI.result: Successfully extends multipole formalism to many-body operator space and classifies monopoles in spinless many-body operators, revealing that electric toroidal monopole (pseudoscalar breaking spatial-inversion symmetry) and magnetic toroidal monopole (time reversal-odd scalar) become active in spinless interacting many-body systems despite being absent in spinless one-body hybrid orbital space.
AI.conclusion: The developed framework provides systematic classification of many-body operators in interacting fermionic systems, revealing new types of monopole order parameters that emerge only in many-body contexts, advancing the understanding of composite order parameters in strongly correlated systems.

title: Ab-initio superfluid weight and superconducting penetration depth
comment: 12 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to Physical Review B as a regular article on the 2nd of March 2026
summary:
Machine learning and high-throughput screening approaches to superconductor discovery require physically meaningful descriptors that capture essential physics while remaining computationally tractable. The superfluid weight is an ideal descriptor as it is a prerequisite for superconductivity, determines the magnetic penetration depth and the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition temperature in two-dimensional materials, may limit the critical temperature in unconventional superconductors through phase coherence, and reveals quantum geometric contributions to supercurrent transport. We develop a computationally efficient framework for calculating the zero-temperature, mean-field superfluid weight for uniform pairing from density functional theory band structures and Bloch wavefunctions. We separately evaluate the conventional contribution from band curvature and the geometric contribution from quantum geometry. To validate the method, we calculate London penetration depths for a few conventional superconductors (Al, Pb, Nb, MgB$_2$, LuRu$_3$B$_2$ and YRu$_3$B$_2$) and find good agreement with experiment after accounting for nonlocal corrections, strong-coupling effects, and sample quality.
  The conventional contribution dominates by orders of magnitude in these wide-band materials, as expected. This framework provides a foundation for large-scale screening of superconducting candidates and exploring quantum geometric effects in unconventional superconductors.

AI.tldr: A computational framework for efficiently calculating superfluid weight from DFT band structures, separating conventional and geometric contributions, validated on conventional superconductors with good experimental agreement.
AI.motivation: Machine learning and high-throughput screening for superconductor discovery require physically meaningful yet computationally efficient descriptors. Superfluid weight is ideal as it captures essential superconductivity physics, determines key properties like penetration depth and transition temperatures, and reveals quantum geometric effects in unconventional superconductors.
AI.method: Developed a computationally efficient framework for calculating zero-temperature, mean-field superfluid weight for uniform pairing from density functional theory (DFT) band structures and Bloch wavefunctions. The method separately evaluates conventional contribution from band curvature and geometric contribution from quantum geometry.
AI.result: Validated the method by calculating London penetration depths for conventional superconductors (Al, Pb, Nb, MgB₂, LuRu₃B₂, YRu₃B₂) with good agreement to experiment after accounting for nonlocal corrections, strong-coupling effects, and sample quality. Conventional contribution dominates by orders of magnitude in these wide-band materials.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a foundation for large-scale screening of superconducting candidates and exploring quantum geometric effects in unconventional superconductors, enabling efficient computational discovery and analysis of superconducting materials.

title: Engineering photomagnetism in collinear van der Waals antiferromagnets
summary: Achieving efficient ultrafast optical control of antiferromagnetic spin dynamics is a central goal for next-generation high-speed THz spintronic and magnonic devices. Resonant optical pumping of crystal-field-split d-d orbital multiplets in magnetic TM ions directly modulates exchange and spin-orbit interactions, inducing large-amplitude coherent spin precession. However, such effects are limited to a handful of systems and there is no general strategy to enhance d-d photomagnetism in antiferromagnets. Here, we demonstrate the engineering of photomagnetism via TM-ion doping in collinear van der Waals antiferromagnets. In Mn$_{1-x}$Ni$_x$PS$_3$, small amounts of Ni$^{2+}$ activate a strong photomagnetic response while largely preserving the Néel ground state. Even 10% Ni boosts the response by more than an order of magnitude compared to pure MnPS$_3$, with resonant pumping of Ni$^{2+}$ d-d transitions driving large-amplitude coherent spin precession and providing helicity-dependent phase control. Tuning the pump energy across the full Mn$_{1-x}$Ni$_x$PS$_3$ composition range shows that Ni excitations remain effective across competing Néel and zig-zag antiferromagnetic states while supporting tunable-frequency coherent spin precession. These results establish TM-ion doping as a versatile strategy to harness orbital multiplet excitations for ultrafast, low-dissipation spin control in van der Waals antiferromagnets.

AI.tldr: Transition metal ion doping (Ni into MnPS₃) dramatically enhances photomagnetic response in van der Waals antiferromagnets, enabling large-amplitude coherent spin precession via resonant d-d orbital excitation.
AI.motivation: There is a need for efficient ultrafast optical control of antiferromagnetic spin dynamics for next-generation high-speed THz spintronic and magnonic devices. While resonant optical pumping of crystal-field-split d-d orbital multiplets can modulate exchange and spin-orbit interactions, such effects are limited to few systems with no general strategy to enhance d-d photomagnetism in antiferromagnets.
AI.method: Engineering photomagnetism via transition metal ion doping in collinear van der Waals antiferromagnets. Specifically, doping MnPS₃ with Ni²⁺ ions (Mn₁₋ₓNiₓPS₃) to activate strong photomagnetic response while largely preserving the Néel ground state. Resonant pumping of Ni²⁺ d-d transitions drives the spin dynamics.
AI.result: Even 10% Ni doping boosts photomagnetic response by more than an order of magnitude compared to pure MnPS₃. Ni²⁺ d-d transitions drive large-amplitude coherent spin precession with helicity-dependent phase control. Ni excitations remain effective across competing Néel and zig-zag antiferromagnetic states while supporting tunable-frequency coherent spin precession.
AI.conclusion: Transition metal ion doping establishes a versatile strategy to harness orbital multiplet excitations for ultrafast, low-dissipation spin control in van der Waals antiferromagnets, enabling enhanced photomagnetic response and coherent spin manipulation.

title: Non-Collinear and Non-Coplanar Magnetic Orders in 1/1 Periodic Approximant to the Icosahedral Quasicrystal
comment: 15 pages, 19 figures, Selected as JPSJ Editor's Choice, Selected as JPS Hot Topics
summary: Ground-state properties of rare-earth based 1/1 periodic approximants of icosahedral quasicrystal are clarified theoretically on the basis of an effective model for magnetism taking into account uniaxial anisotropy arising from crystalline electric field. By performing numerically-exact calculation on the 1/1 approximant crystal with a lattice constant $a$=14.725 Å, we have determined the ground-state phase diagram for ferromagnetic interactions. The result shows that eight kinds of noncollinear and noncoplanar magnetic structures are stabilized, whose magnetic space groups are identified as $I_{\rm P}m'\bar{3}'$, $C2'/m'$ and $R\bar{3}$. We have clarified the degeneracy of each ground state, which is expected to be reflected in the numbers of the domains. By analyzing each state, the magnetic as well as topological properties are revealed. Our results are shown to explain the measured magnetic structures in the 1/1 approximants and the effective model is discussed to be useful for understanding the magnetic structures and their topological properties in broad range of rare-earth based 1/1 approximants.

AI.tldr: Theoretical study reveals eight noncollinear/noncoplanar magnetic ground states in rare-earth 1/1 approximants with ferromagnetic interactions, explaining experimental observations and topological properties.
AI.motivation: To clarify ground-state properties of rare-earth based 1/1 periodic approximants of icosahedral quasicrystals by developing an effective model that accounts for crystalline electric field-induced uniaxial anisotropy.
AI.method: Developed an effective magnetic model incorporating uniaxial anisotropy from crystalline electric field, then performed numerically-exact calculations on 1/1 approximant crystal with lattice constant a=14.725 Å to determine ground-state phase diagram for ferromagnetic interactions.
AI.result: Identified eight distinct noncollinear and noncoplanar magnetic structures stabilized in the ground state, with magnetic space groups IPm'3', C2'/m', and R3. Determined degeneracy of each ground state (reflected in domain numbers) and analyzed magnetic and topological properties.
AI.conclusion: The theoretical results successfully explain measured magnetic structures in 1/1 approximants, and the effective model provides a useful framework for understanding magnetic structures and topological properties across a broad range of rare-earth based 1/1 approximants.

title: Flexible Cutoff Learning: Optimizing Machine Learning Potentials After Training
summary: We introduce Flexible Cutoff Learning (FCL), a method for training machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) whose cutoff radii can be adjusted after training. Unlike conventional MLIPs that fix the cutoff radius during training, FCL models are trained by randomly sampling cutoff radii independently for each atom. The resulting model can then be deployed with different per-atom cutoff radii depending on the application, enabling application-specific optimization of the accuracy-cost tradeoff. Using a differentiable cost model, these per-atom cutoffs can be optimized for specific target systems after training. We demonstrate FCL with a modified MACE architecture trained on the MAD dataset. For a subset featuring molecular crystals, optimized per-atom cutoffs reduce computational cost by more than 60% while increasing force errors by less than 1%. These results show that FCL enables training of a single general-purpose MLIP that can be adapted to diverse applications through post-training cutoff optimization, eliminating the need for retraining.

AI.tldr: FCL enables training MLIPs with adjustable cutoff radii post-training, allowing application-specific optimization of accuracy-cost tradeoffs without retraining.
AI.motivation: Conventional MLIPs fix cutoff radii during training, limiting flexibility for different applications where computational cost vs. accuracy tradeoffs vary. There's a need for MLIPs that can adapt to specific target systems without retraining.
AI.method: FCL trains MLIPs by randomly sampling cutoff radii independently for each atom during training. The method uses a modified MACE architecture trained on the MAD dataset, with a differentiable cost model to optimize per-atom cutoffs for specific target systems after training.
AI.result: For molecular crystal subsets, optimized per-atom cutoffs reduce computational cost by >60% while increasing force errors by <1%. This demonstrates significant efficiency gains with minimal accuracy loss.
AI.conclusion: FCL enables training of a single general-purpose MLIP that can be adapted to diverse applications through post-training cutoff optimization, eliminating the need for retraining and allowing application-specific optimization of accuracy-cost tradeoffs.

title: Pairing and charge distribution in Emery ladders preserving the ratio of Cu to O atoms
summary: We study the Emery model (three-band Hubbard model) for superconducting cuprates on three distinct ladder-like lattices that are supercell of the CuO$_2$ plane and thus preserve the ratio of copper to oxygen atoms. Using the density-matrix renormalization group method we confirm that these Emery ladders are charge-transfer insulators for the hole concentration corresponding to undoped cuprates but become Luther-Emery liquids with enhanced pairing correlations upon doping. The preservation of the Cu to O ratio allows us to study the distribution of charges between these atoms in the Luther-Emery phase. We show that these Emery ladders can describe the relations between charge distribution, pairing strength, and interactions that have been observed in the Emery model on two-dimensional clusters and in experiments.

AI.tldr: Emery ladders (3-band Hubbard model) on CuO₂ supercell lattices show charge-transfer insulating behavior at half-filling and transition to Luther-Emery liquids with enhanced pairing upon doping, revealing relationships between charge distribution, pairing strength, and interactions.
AI.motivation: To understand the superconducting properties of cuprates by studying the Emery model on ladder-like lattices that preserve the Cu:O ratio, enabling investigation of charge distribution between copper and oxygen atoms in the Luther-Emery phase.
AI.method: Used density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) method to study the three-band Hubbard (Emery) model on three distinct ladder-like lattices that are supercells of the CuO₂ plane, preserving the copper to oxygen atom ratio.
AI.result: Emery ladders are charge-transfer insulators at hole concentration corresponding to undoped cuprates, but become Luther-Emery liquids with enhanced pairing correlations upon doping. The study reveals relationships between charge distribution, pairing strength, and interactions consistent with 2D cluster studies and experiments.
AI.conclusion: Emery ladders provide a valuable framework for studying the relationships between charge distribution, pairing correlations, and interactions in cuprate superconductors, bridging insights from 2D cluster studies and experimental observations.

title: Structural and Optical Characteristics of beta-Ga2O3 Implanted with Rare Earth Ions
summary:
We investigated the structural evolution and optical properties of beta-Ga2O3 crystals implanted with different rare-earth (RE) ions using channeling Rutherford Backscattering Spectrometry, Positron Annihilation, Photoluminescence, and Photoluminescence Excitation spectroscopies. The studies reveal that implantation-induced disorder, accompanying phase transitions, and post-annealing structural recovery are largely insensitive to the implanted RE species. The defect microstructure is also found to be similar for all implanted RE ions.
  Thermal annealing does not completely remove radiation-induced defects but instead drives their rearrangement into larger defect complexes. Unimplanted (virgin) beta-Ga2O3 exhibits strong UV-visible emission attributed to oxygen vacancies, whereas the introduction of RE ions produces additional emission lines originating from electronic transitions within RE3+ ions.
  The results indicate that RE3+ ions are excited through the host conduction band, followed by non-radiative relaxation to the 4f excited states and radiative decay to the respective ground states. Fluence-dependent studies of Yb3+ reveal the onset of concentration quenching, while RE-related emission remains efficient even in the presence of substantial lattice disorder.
  These findings provide new insight into defect evolution in ion-implanted beta-Ga2O3 and clarify the excitation mechanisms of RE3+ ions, offering guidance for optimizing the optical performance of beta-Ga2O3:RE materials.

AI.tldr: Rare-earth ion implantation in beta-Ga2O3 shows similar structural damage and defect evolution regardless of RE species, with RE3+ ions excited via host conduction band and efficient emission even with lattice disorder.
AI.motivation: To understand the structural evolution and optical properties of beta-Ga2O3 crystals implanted with different rare-earth ions, and to clarify the excitation mechanisms of RE3+ ions in this host material.
AI.method: Used channeling Rutherford Backscattering Spectrometry, Positron Annihilation, Photoluminescence, and Photoluminescence Excitation spectroscopies to study beta-Ga2O3 crystals implanted with various RE ions, with thermal annealing treatments and fluence-dependent studies.
AI.result: Implantation-induced disorder, phase transitions, and post-annealing recovery are insensitive to RE species; defect microstructure is similar for all RE ions. Thermal annealing rearranges defects into larger complexes rather than removing them. RE3+ ions are excited through host conduction band with non-radiative relaxation to 4f states. Yb3+ shows concentration quenching, but RE emission remains efficient despite lattice disorder.
AI.conclusion: The study provides new insights into defect evolution in ion-implanted beta-Ga2O3 and clarifies RE3+ excitation mechanisms, offering guidance for optimizing optical performance of beta-Ga2O3:RE materials for potential optoelectronic applications.

title: Electronic Structure and Resonant Circular Dichroism of La$_{0.7}$Sr$_{0.3}$MnO$_3$ from Soft X-ray Angle-Resolved Photoemission
summary: Coupling between spin, orbital, charge, and lattice degrees of freedom in transition-metal oxides produces a variety of electronic and magnetic phenomena of importance for future technologies. Here, we explore the electronic band structure of a (111)-oriented La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 thin film through soft X-ray angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). The measurements agree with the electronic band structure calculated with density functional theory using Hubbard U correction. Furthermore, we probe the circular dichroism in ARPES, and observe a pronounced momentum- resolved magnetic circular dichroism in resonant photoemission from the Mn L-edge. The approach combines the momentum- and spin-selectivity of ARPES and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism, respectively, which could provide a useful approach for the study of unconventional magnetism.

AI.tldr: Soft X-ray ARPES study of (111)-oriented La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 thin film reveals electronic band structure and momentum-resolved magnetic circular dichroism from Mn L-edge.
AI.motivation: Transition-metal oxides exhibit complex coupling between spin, orbital, charge, and lattice degrees of freedom, producing diverse electronic and magnetic phenomena relevant for future technologies. Understanding these interactions requires advanced spectroscopic techniques.
AI.method: Used soft X-ray angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) on (111)-oriented La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 thin film. Combined with density functional theory calculations using Hubbard U correction. Probed circular dichroism in ARPES, specifically momentum-resolved magnetic circular dichroism in resonant photoemission from Mn L-edge.
AI.result: ARPES measurements agree with DFT+U calculated electronic band structure. Observed pronounced momentum-resolved magnetic circular dichroism in resonant photoemission from Mn L-edge, demonstrating the combination of momentum- and spin-selectivity.
AI.conclusion: The approach combining ARPES (momentum-selectivity) and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (spin-selectivity) provides a useful method for studying unconventional magnetism in complex oxide systems.

title: A fully solution-processed organic microcavity laser in the strong light-matter coupling regime
summary: Solid-state semiconductor lasers underpin technologies from telecommunications and data storage to sensing, medical diagnostics, and emerging quantum communication. Polaritons-hybrid exciton-photon states have further extended this reach, enabling room-temperature quantum effects such as low-threshold lasing and single-photon nonlinearities. Organic semiconductors are ideal for polaritonics due to their large exciton binding energy, strong optical nonlinearities, and straightforward processing, making them attractive for both classical and quantum photonics. While solution-processed organic films have been widely explored, their optical cavities have almost always been fabricated using vacuum deposition, limiting the realization of truly scalable and low-cost devices. Here, we report the first organic laser microcavities fabricated entirely by solution processing, which operate in the strong coupling regimeThe resulting platform can be driven reliably to high excitation densities, where we observe a reversible, interaction-driven redistribution of the polariton condensate, revealing a distinct polariton lasing behaviour in organic microcavities. Together, the fabrication approach and the observed lasing dynamics establish a route toward scalable polaritonic and quantum photonic technologies and provide new opportunities for studying nonlinear polariton physics in organic systems.

AI.tldr: First demonstration of fully solution-processed organic laser microcavities operating in strong coupling regime, showing polariton lasing with reversible interaction-driven condensate redistribution.
AI.motivation: Organic semiconductors are ideal for polaritonics due to large exciton binding energy and strong nonlinearities, but current fabrication relies on vacuum deposition, limiting scalability and cost-effectiveness for truly scalable quantum photonic technologies.
AI.method: Developed the first organic laser microcavities fabricated entirely by solution processing, operating in the strong coupling regime, enabling study of polariton dynamics at high excitation densities.
AI.result: Successfully demonstrated strong coupling operation with reliable high excitation density driving, observed reversible interaction-driven redistribution of polariton condensate, revealing distinct polariton lasing behavior in organic microcavities.
AI.conclusion: The fabrication approach and observed lasing dynamics establish a route toward scalable polaritonic and quantum photonic technologies while providing new opportunities for studying nonlinear polariton physics in organic systems.

title: Generalized Reduced-Density-Matrix Quantum Monte Carlo Gives Access to More
summary: In quantum Monte Carlo (QMC), what can be measured efficiently is largely determined by what is sampled. When the sampled object is the partition function, a broad class of observables, including general off-diagonal operators, is typically unavailable as direct estimators. In this article, we introduce a paradigm shift by replacing the partition function with a generalized reduced density matrix (GRDM) as the simulated object. This reformulation removes the measurement bottleneck at its source and extends the dimensional-reduction advantage of reduced descriptions from static quantities to dynamical observables, thereby enabling much richer information extraction. As substantial demonstrations, the framework allows the directed-loop algorithm to measure both equal-time and imaginary-time off-diagonal observables, with the latter giving direct access to dynamical spectra. It also enables measurements of Rényi-1 correlators that diagnose strong-to-weak symmetry breaking in mixed states. This work establishes a unified framework for holographic characterization within QMC.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a paradigm shift in quantum Monte Carlo by replacing partition function sampling with generalized reduced density matrix sampling, enabling efficient measurement of previously inaccessible off-diagonal and dynamical observables.
AI.motivation: Current QMC methods face limitations in measuring general off-diagonal operators and dynamical observables when sampling the partition function, creating a measurement bottleneck that restricts information extraction.
AI.method: Reformulate QMC by replacing the partition function with a generalized reduced density matrix (GRDM) as the simulated object, extending dimensional-reduction advantages to dynamical observables and enabling direct measurement of previously inaccessible quantities.
AI.result: The framework enables directed-loop algorithms to measure both equal-time and imaginary-time off-diagonal observables (providing access to dynamical spectra) and allows measurement of Rényi-1 correlators for diagnosing symmetry breaking in mixed states.
AI.conclusion: This work establishes a unified framework for holographic characterization within QMC, fundamentally changing what can be efficiently measured by addressing the measurement bottleneck at its source through GRDM sampling.

title: Frontiers of atom probe tomography physics, data processing, and analysis
comment: 43 pages, 7 multicomponent figures, summary of workshop
summary: Atom probe tomography (APT) fills a crucial need in the characterization workflow of materials by its ability to inform the 3D chemical microstructure at the nanoscale. As with any characterization techniques, APT has strengths and limitations that inform the interpretation of the data. Therefore, a challenge for the materials characterization community, and the APT community in particular, is the need to establish repeatable and reproducible workflows around the APT data acquisition, reconstruction, analysis, and sharing, in order to inform interpretation. Data interpretation also requires the continued development of our understanding of the physical processes responsible for field evaporation. We review recent developments in the experimental analysis of field evaporation and in the modeling of field evaporation leading to new understanding of common artifacts observed in reconstructed data. We then discuss current challenges with data analysis, translation of results, and data interpretation in the absence of community-agreed standards, and therefore, the crucial need for standardization at every stage of APT research, from data collection all the way to data reporting. This perspective is a summary of the invited presentations and discussions that took place during a workshop (August 4-5, 2024, Alexandria, Virginia, USA).

AI.tldr: This perspective paper reviews recent developments in atom probe tomography (APT), highlighting challenges in data interpretation and the need for standardized workflows across acquisition, reconstruction, analysis, and reporting.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to address the lack of standardized workflows in APT characterization, which hinders repeatable and reproducible data interpretation, and to emphasize the need for community-agreed standards to improve reliability and comparability of APT results.
AI.method: The paper reviews recent developments in field evaporation analysis and modeling, summarizes workshop discussions, and examines current challenges in APT data analysis, translation, and interpretation.
AI.result: The review identifies key artifacts in APT reconstructions, highlights gaps in understanding field evaporation processes, and documents the absence of community standards that currently limit reliable data interpretation.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that establishing standardized workflows at every stage of APT research—from data collection to reporting—is crucial for advancing materials characterization and ensuring reliable, reproducible results.

title: Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya-driven instabilities in square-kagome quantum antiferromagnets
summary: Decorated square-kagome quantum antiferromagnets provide a natural setting in which strong frustration, lattice decoration, and spin-orbit-induced anisotropy compete on comparable energy scales. Here we show that in Na$_6$Cu$_7$BiO$_4$(PO$_4$)$_4$Cl$_3$ the coupling ($J_{10}$) which links the decorating Cu(3) sites to the square-kagome backbone, stabilizes the gapped quantum-paramagnetic regime, while symmetry-allowed Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interactions systematically suppress the minimum spinon gap $Δ_{\mathrm{spinon}}$ and drive the system toward magnetic condensation. To establish this, we combine ab initio calculation of the DM vectors with a generalized Schwinger-boson self-consistent mean-field theory that treats singlet and triplet hopping/pairing channels on equal footing. As a benchmark, the isotropic square-kagome Heisenberg model exhibits four competing low-energy saddle points distinguished by their Wilson-loop fluxes and by characteristic static and dynamical structure-factor fingerprints. A minimal DM perturbation does not qualitatively reshape this competing landscape, but already enhances the tendency towards order. For the realistic decorated Hamiltonian, finite-size scaling of $Δ_{\mathrm{spinon}}$ together with momentum-resolved structure factors identifies $J_{10}$ (exchange with decorating Cu) as the control parameter of the gapped regime and shows that the full symmetry-allowed DM pattern shifts the system further toward condensation. Our results place Na$_6$Cu$_7$BiO$_4$(PO$_4$)$_4$Cl$_3$ in close proximity to a magnetic instability and provide experimentally testable predictions for anisotropy-enhanced soft modes in decorated square-kagome materials.

AI.tldr: Decorated square-kagome quantum antiferromagnet Na₆Cu₇BiO₄(PO₄)₄Cl₃ shows competition between frustration, lattice decoration, and spin-orbit anisotropy. The coupling linking decorating sites stabilizes gapped quantum paramagnetic regime, while Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions suppress spinon gap and drive toward magnetic condensation.
AI.motivation: To understand how competing energy scales (frustration, lattice decoration, spin-orbit anisotropy) determine the quantum magnetic properties of decorated square-kagome materials, specifically Na₆Cu₇BiO₄(PO₄)₄Cl₃, and to identify control parameters for the gapped quantum-paramagnetic regime.
AI.method: Combined ab initio calculation of DM vectors with generalized Schwinger-boson self-consistent mean-field theory that treats singlet and triplet hopping/pairing channels equally. Finite-size scaling of spinon gap and momentum-resolved structure factors used to analyze the system.
AI.result: The coupling J₁₀ linking decorating Cu(3) sites to square-kagome backbone stabilizes gapped quantum-paramagnetic regime. DM interactions systematically suppress minimum spinon gap Δ_spinon and drive system toward magnetic condensation. The isotropic square-kagome Heisenberg model shows four competing low-energy saddle points with distinct Wilson-loop fluxes and structure-factor fingerprints. Realistic decorated Hamiltonian shows J₁₀ as control parameter of gapped regime, with full symmetry-allowed DM pattern shifting system further toward condensation.
AI.conclusion: Na₆Cu₇BiO₄(PO₄)₄Cl₃ is in close proximity to a magnetic instability, with DM interactions enhancing tendency toward order. The study provides experimentally testable predictions for anisotropy-enhanced soft modes in decorated square-kagome materials.

title: Electron-phonon physics at the exascale: A hybrid MPI-GPU-OpenMP framework for scalable Wannier interpolation
comment: 30 pages, 13 figures; accepted in npj Computational Materials
summary: We demonstrate a highly efficient GPU implementation of the Wannier interpolation of electron-phonon matrix elements in the EPW code. Building on a systematic analysis of the computational complexity of the algorithm for electron-phonon interpolation, we designed a GPU porting strategy that integrates naturally into the current EPW implementation, and is seamlessly portable to NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs. We demonstrate this development via extensive benchmarks on conventional semiconductors such as silicon and monolayer MoS$_2$, as well as a large-scale application to topological stanene nanoribbons of width as large as 20nm, which was intractable with previous implementations. Compared to the single MPI parallelization scheme of EPW v5.9, the resulting hybrid MPI-GPU-OpenMP scheme achieves up to 29-fold speedup on leadership-class supercomputers equipped with NVIDIA and Intel accelerators, namely Vista at the Texas Advanced Computing Center, Perlmutter at the National Energy Research Scientific Computing Center, and Aurora at the Argonne Leadership Computing Facility. This framework also achieves nearly ideal scalability up to thousands of GPU nodes on the Aurora supercomputer. With this development, EPW is ready to support electron-phonon physics calculations on exascale platforms.

AI.tldr: GPU-accelerated implementation of Wannier interpolation for electron-phonon matrix elements in EPW code achieves up to 29× speedup and scales to thousands of GPU nodes on exascale platforms.
AI.motivation: Previous implementations of electron-phonon interpolation in EPW were computationally limited, making large-scale applications like 20nm topological stanene nanoribbons intractable. The need for efficient calculations on exascale platforms motivated GPU acceleration.
AI.method: Systematic analysis of computational complexity followed by GPU porting strategy integrated into current EPW implementation. Developed hybrid MPI-GPU-OpenMP scheme that is portable to NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs. Benchmarked on leadership-class supercomputers (Vista, Perlmutter, Aurora).
AI.result: Achieved up to 29-fold speedup compared to single MPI parallelization in EPW v5.9. Demonstrated nearly ideal scalability up to thousands of GPU nodes on Aurora supercomputer. Enabled previously intractable large-scale applications like 20nm topological stanene nanoribbons.
AI.conclusion: The GPU-accelerated EPW implementation is ready for electron-phonon physics calculations on exascale platforms, overcoming previous computational limitations and enabling large-scale applications.

title: Two-Body Solution and Instabilities along Streda Lines in Moire Flat Bands
summary: Moire minibands in twisted homobilayer semiconductors can, under suitable approximations, be modeled as a pair of Landau levels with opposite Chern numbers. This provides a minimal model for searching novel topological states in a time-reversal-symmetric Hamiltonian. In this work, we investigate the effects of an external magnetic field in this model. We study the many-body ground state in the density-magnetic-field (n-B) plane along the dn/dB = \pm1/Phi0 Streda line with Hartree-Fock approximation.
